doe-osti-3818575-idms-method-development:
Savannah River report SRNL-TR-2026-00551, dated July 29, 2026, sets out a workflow for isotope dilution mass spectrometry assays. Six authors are printed: Shelby Bowden, Kyle Samperton, Ashlee Swindle, Heather Brant, Matthew Harrell, and Elizabeth Pettitt. The method measures tungsten, lead, thorium, and uranium levels with very low doubt. A known enriched spike is mixed into each sample, and isotope ratios do the rest. Because ratios rule, the method shrugs off instrument drift that weakens plain signal-based assays.

Each element gets its own clean-up path. Tungsten passes two columns to shed matrix and rival elements. Lead is pulled out on an anion exchange resin. Uranium and thorium ride one shared specialty column. Enriched spikes for all four elements were made, checked, and calibrated in house. The workflow supports nuclear forensic reference materials, where assay trust matters most.
